title: Tenali Raman Tale 142 (தமிழ்)

full_text:
A sudden panic struck the northern agricultural district of Anegundi:
A rumor spread that an ancient curse had turned the communal irrigation lake completely salty!
Farmers tasted the water at the southern weir and spat it out in horror: it was intensely salty, threatening to kill their rice crops!
A corrupt grain speculator named Bhupati immediately offered to buy all the farmers’ lands at pennies on the dollar, claiming the valley was ruined forever.

King Krishnadevaraya sent Tenali Raman to investigate the catastrophe.

Tenali rode to the lake.
He tasted the water at the southern weir: indeed, it was intensely salty.
However, Tenali rowed a small wooden boat across to the northern inlet where the mountain mountain stream entered the lake:
He dipped his cup into the water:
The northern inlet water was completely, delightfully sweet, fresh, and cold!

Tenali reasoned:
'If a curse had salted the lake, the entire body of water would be uniformly saline.
Why is the water fresh at the northern inlet, but salty only at the southern weir?'

Tenali inspected the stone masonry of the southern weir.
Beneath the water line, Tenali’s boat paddle struck something soft.
He dove into the shallows:
Submerged behind the stone sluice gate were thirty enormous burlap sacks of coarse sea salt, slowly dissolving into the outflow current!
Tied to the sacks was an iron tag stamped with the warehouse seal of none other than **Grain Speculator Bhupati**!

Bhupati had dumped thirty cartloads of cheap sea salt into the weir to create a temporary panic, hoping to buy the fertile lands for nothing!

Tenali hauled the salt sacks out of the water, arrested Bhupati on the spot, and had the sluice gate flushed with fresh mountain water.
Within two hours, the outflow ran completely sweet and fresh again!
The farmers cheered, their lands were saved, and Bhupati’s entire grain empire was confiscated to fund free agricultural schools.
King Krishnadevaraya praised Tenali Raman’s sharp scientific logic, which saw through speculative fraud to protect the innocent.
moral: False rumors designed to spark speculative panics are extinguished by scientific investigation. [TA]
